Problem 1: LU factorization
Let $A \in \mathbb { R } ^ { n }$ be a real tridiagonal matrix

$$
A = \left[ \begin{array}{c c c c c} \alpha_ {1} & \gamma_ {2} & & & \\ \beta_ {1} & \alpha_ {2} & \gamma_ {3} & & \\ & \beta_ {2} & \alpha_ {3} & \ddots & \\ & & \ddots & \ddots & \gamma_ {n} \\ & & & \beta_ {n - 1} & \alpha_ {n} \end{array} \right].
$$

Consider applying the LU factorization with partial pivoting to this A to get $L U = P A$ . The algorithm (“Algorithm 3”) proceeds as follows, where L and U are stored in the lower and upper parts of A respectively:

code_body: Algorithm 3: LU decomposition with partial pivoting 1 for $k = 1, \ldots, n - 1$ do 2 Find the smallest index L such that $|A(l, k)| = \max_{k \leq i \leq n} |A(i, k)|$ ; 3 Swap $A(k, 1 : n)$ and $A(l, 1 : n)$ and record the pair $(k, l)$ ; 4 for $i = k + 1, \ldots, n$ do 5 $A(i, k) = A(i, k)/A(k, k)$ ; 6 $A(i, k + 1 : n) = A(i, k + 1 : n) - A(i, k) * A(k, k + 1 : n)$
